name: Forestiera

study_strategy.warning: F. angustifolia and F. pubescens both have elbow-like branches and drupes. Drought, pruning and leaf age can obscure differences. Existing F. angustifolia image metadata points to a Guaiacum source and is not cleared as a teaching anchor.
teaching_order: Locate a mid-stem node and compare leaf attachment (phyllotaxy).
Measure several mature leaf blades at equivalent positions, upper and lower faces.
Photograph a leaf edge side-on to verify revolute versus flatter margin; check for hairs without assuming their absence.
Confirm tiny apetalous flowers or drupes when present; do not use branching angles or season alone.

quick_split: F. pubescens — broader elliptic/ovate leaves, some pubescence, winter-deciduous.
F. angustifolia — tiny narrow linear leathery leaves, densely twiggy, evergreen/semi-evergreen or drought-deciduous.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Inspect a leafy mid-stem twig: paired/subopposite leaves on rigid, often elbow-like side branches. Then check the small apetalous flowers or dark one-seeded drupes. Do not identify by right-angle branching alone.
shared_traits: Woody shrubs with stiff, often paired angled branchlets
Small, simple, usually opposite to subopposite leaves
Small, inconspicuous flowers without showy petals, often appearing before new leaves
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Leaflessness, drought and pruning obscure habit; use comparable mature leaves from the same stem position.

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Very narrow, linear, leathery; blade margins often rolled under (revolute)
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Much broader elliptic, ovate, obovate to broadly lanceolate

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Firm, narrow blades, often revolute; pubescence not the principal clue
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Often scattered short hairs; broad blades with flatter margins

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Evergreen to semievergreen in favorable conditions, drought-deciduous when stressed
Very dense intricate twiggy habit with stiff near-right-angle branches
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Paired rigid lateral branches also make elbow-like angles

species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera angustifolia: Small apetalous flowers before leaf flush; dark one-seeded drupes
species_comparison_matrix.Forestiera pubescens: Small apetalous flowers before leaf flush; dark purple drupes
species_comparison_matrix.weight: confirms genus, not a strong split

species_key.look: mid-stem mature leaves in focus, with ruler
species_key.if: linear, leathery, very narrow leaves, often rolled at margin

species_key.look: mid-stem mature leaves in focus, with ruler
species_key.if: broad elliptic/ovate/obovate leaves, sometimes visibly hairy

species_key.look: repeat on several shoots and check phenology
species_key.if: leaf shape conflicts or shrub is defoliated
species_key.then: Do not force species ID; photograph fruit/flowers, winter shoots, and revisit at leaf-out.

overlap_and_cautions: Both species make elbow-like paired branchlets; branch angles are not a species separator.
Drought can defoliate F. angustifolia; deciduous versus evergreen is seasonal support, not an absolute rule.
Young shoots and shade leaves can differ in width; compare mature leaves from matching mid-stem positions.
The dark drupe and apetalous flowers support genus recognition but alone do not separate these two species.
Avoid claiming an exact blade-width cutoff without independently verified measurements.

local_lookalike_routing.separate: Compare larger paired leaves and flower/fruit clusters; Forestiera typically has tiny apetalous flowers and a small drupe.
Check leaf arrangement and twig armature; do not rely on a skeletal shrub silhouette alone.
Ash has compound leaves and samaras; Forestiera has simple leaves and drupes.

targeted_handoff.question: Find an authoritative regional key with comparable measured mature leaf blade widths and confirm whether pubescence/revolute margins hold across local populations before adding numerical cutoffs.

look_here_first: At a leafy node, confirm SIMPLE opposite/subopposite leaves on a woody twig. Next compare fully grown leaves at the SAME stem position: narrow, leathery, often rolled-edge leaves favor F. angustifolia; broad elliptic/ovate blades favor F. pubescens. Then look for tiny PETAL-LESS flowers before leaf-out or small dark DRUPES. Elbow-like branching confirms neither species by itself.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: At a leafy node, confirm SIMPLE opposite/subopposite leaves on a woody twig. Next compare fully grown leaves at the SAME stem position: narrow, leathery, often rolled-edge leaves favor F. angustifolia; broad elliptic/ovate blades favor F. pubescens. Then look for tiny PETAL-LESS flowers before leaf-out or small dark DRUPES. Elbow-like branching confirms neither species by itself.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Look at the same spot on the twig: leaves occur as pairs or nearly paired, rather than singly alternating.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: sharp twig node with intact petiole attachments on both species
shared_structure_examples.why: A useful entry point to Forestiera, but not a species split; compare Oleaceae privets and other opposite-leaved shrubs.

shared_structure_examples.plain: A simple leaf has one blade. 'Revolute' means the edge curls underneath, best seen from the side.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched fully expanded leaves on millimeter grid plus edge-profile macro of F. angustifolia
shared_structure_examples.why: Very narrow, leathery, often rolled leaves favor F. angustifolia; broader, flatter leaves favor F. pubescens.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Tiny flowers may lack petals; pollen-bearing stamens can be visible on leafless spring twigs.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: close flower macro showing twig attachment and stamens, with an intact whole branch for context
shared_structure_examples.why: Helps separate Forestiera from Ligustrum, whose small flowers have a conspicuous four-lobed fused corolla. Flowers alone do not split these Forestiera species.

shared_structure_examples.plain: A small dark fruit with a fleshy outer layer around a hard seed.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: mature attached fruit cluster with fruit stalk and nearby leaves
shared_structure_examples.why: Confirms the genus and separates it from Fraxinus, which makes winged samaras; fruit color alone does not separate the two Forestiera species.

confusable_genera.distinction: Opposite simple leaves and dark fruits can resemble Forestiera, but Ligustrum flowers have a four-lobed fused corolla; Forestiera flowers are tiny and generally apetalous.
Ashes have pinnately compound leaves and one-winged samaras; Forestiera has simple leaves and fleshy drupes.
Check alternate versus opposite leaf attachment and inspect twig armature; thorny silhouettes alone are not decisive.

comparison_cards.title: Narrowleaf versus downy Forestiera: measure the leaves
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare several fully grown leaves from similar mid-stem positions at the same magnification. F. angustifolia has very narrow, often rolled-edge leathery blades; F. pubescens has much broader elliptic, ovate or obovate blades.
comparison_cards.difference: Leaf shape/relative width and margin profile are stronger than shared elbow branching; do not invent a numerical width threshold without a regional key.
photo_requirements: matched upper and lower leaf faces with millimeter scale
side-on F. angustifolia leaf margin showing recurved edge
comparison_cards.caution: Drought-stressed and juvenile foliage changes leaf size. F. angustifolia's existing provisional image may depict Guaiacum, not Forestiera; do not use it as proof.

comparison_cards.title: Forestiera or privet? Inspect the actual flower
comparison_cards.look_here_first: On flowering twigs look for inconspicuous apetalous Forestiera flowers versus the four-lobed tubular corolla of Ligustrum. On fruiting twigs confirm attached drupes, but remember both genera can have dark fruit.
comparison_cards.difference: Apetalous flowers on short spring twig clusters versus corollate privet panicles; leaf arrangement alone is shared.
photo_requirements: F. pubescens flower macro with visible stamens and twig insertion
F. angustifolia confirmed exact-species flower macro
Ligustrum four-lobed corolla macro at matched scale
fruit close-up with attached pedicel and foliage
comparison_cards.caution: Flowering stage and sex of plant can change visible floral structures; do not imply one photograph shows every reproductive character.
